rank_rule: Rank 1 is the highest observed value for the selected index.

families.label: Export competition
families.description: Chinese exports displaced from the U.S. are redirected to third markets, where they erode other exporters' sales.

families.label: Export similarity
families.description: How closely a country's export basket resembles China's. Descriptive, and shown in the paper to be a weak guide to actual exposure.

families.label: Import competition
families.description: Redirected Chinese goods raise import penetration at home, squeezing domestic import-competing producers.

families.label: Import similarity
families.description: How closely a country's imports from China resemble what the U.S. imports from China. Descriptive rather than model-based.

families.label: Consumer gains
families.description: Cheaper Chinese imports lower the prices buyers in the destination market pay.

families.label: Sourcing gains
families.description: Cheaper Chinese intermediate inputs cut production costs and strengthen downstream competitiveness.

indices.label: Export Competition Index (ECI)
indices.description: Equation (7). The predicted percentage decline in a country's exports to markets outside the U.S. and China, caused by cheaper Chinese competition there. It multiplies the product-level Chinese price shock by China's penetration of each destination-product market, the importance of that cell in the country's own export basket, and the demand elasticity that governs substitution toward the cheaper Chinese variety.

indices.label: Export Competition Index, product-level (ECI_prod)
indices.description: Equation (8). A coarser version that aggregates across destinations before combining terms, using export-weighted average demand elasticities. It better captures a shock large enough to push Chinese exports into destinations where China sold relatively little in the baseline year. Correlation with the baseline ECI is 0.882.

indices.label: Export Competition Index, long window (ECI_long)
indices.description: The baseline index rebuilt with market shares from 2018 and tariff changes measured from January 2018 to September 2025, rather than the January-to-September 2025 window. Correlation with the baseline ECI is 0.963.

indices.label: Export Competition Index, basic shock (ECI_basic)
indices.description: The baseline index with the model-implied price shock replaced by the transparent proxy: China's baseline export share to the U.S. This drops the demand and supply elasticity estimates and the product-specific tariff change. Correlation with the baseline ECI is 0.974.

indices.label: Export Competition Index, basic shock and full coverage (ECI_basic_full)
indices.description: The basic-shock variant extended to every product where the transparent proxy can be computed, rather than only the products for which the full model-implied shock is available. Widens product coverage at the cost of the elasticity-based refinement.

indices.label: Export Competition Index, trade coverage (ECI_coverage)
indices.description: Diagnostic, not an exposure measure. The share of the country's relevant trade accounted for by products that enter the export competition index. Low values mean the index rests on a narrow slice of the country's trade and should be read with caution.

indices.label: Export Similarity Index (ESI)
indices.description: Equation (2). The Finger-Kreinin overlap between a country's exports and China's, computed across product and destination cells outside the U.S. and China, in the 2023 baseline year. A descriptive measure of trade-basket resemblance. The paper shows it is not a reliable guide to exposure: it is symmetric, and it ignores the size of the product-level shock, Chinese market penetration, substitution elasticities, and incidence weights.

indices.label: Export Similarity Index, destination-weighted (ESI_alt)
indices.description: An export-weighted average of destination-specific similarity indices, rather than a single sum over product-destination cells. Correlation with the baseline ESI is 0.952.

indices.label: Export Similarity Index, products only (ESI_prod)
indices.description: Similarity in the types of products a country exports, regardless of where they are sold. Coarser than the baseline, which conditions on destination as well.

indices.label: Export Similarity Index, destinations only (ESI_dest)
indices.description: Similarity in where a country sells, regardless of which goods it sells there. Coarser than the baseline, which conditions on product as well.

indices.label: Import Competition Index (ICI)
indices.description: Equation (12). The predicted percentage decline in domestic sales of import-competing producers as redirected Chinese goods raise import penetration at home. It weights each product's import pressure by the importance of that sector in domestic sales, proxied by the country's export shares because product-level domestic sales are not available across many countries.

indices.label: Import Competition Index, long window (ICI_long)
indices.description: The baseline index rebuilt with 2018 market shares and tariff changes measured from January 2018 to September 2025.

indices.label: Import Competition Index, basic shock (ICI_basic)
indices.description: The baseline index with the model-implied price shock replaced by China's baseline export share to the U.S., dropping the elasticity and tariff terms.

indices.label: Import Competition Index, basic shock and full coverage (ICI_basic_full)
indices.description: The basic-shock variant extended to every product where the transparent proxy can be computed.

indices.label: Import Competition Index, intermediate inputs (ICI_upstream)
indices.description: The index restricted to intermediate inputs, meaning products with an upstreamness measure above 2. This is the competitive pressure on domestic producers of inputs, the mirror image of the sourcing gains their downstream users enjoy.

indices.label: Import Competition Index, final goods (ICI_downstream)
indices.description: The index restricted to final goods, meaning products with an upstreamness measure below 2. This is the competitive pressure on domestic producers selling close to final demand.

indices.label: Import Competition Index, trade coverage (ICI_coverage)
indices.description: Diagnostic, not an exposure measure. The share of the country's relevant trade accounted for by products that enter the import competition index.

indices.label: Import Similarity Index (ISI)
indices.description: Equation (9). The overlap between what a country imports from China and what the U.S. imports from China, in the 2023 baseline year. The intuition is that a country buying the same Chinese goods the U.S. buys is more likely to receive redirected Chinese exports. The paper finds this is a poor guide to import-competition incidence: across the 110 sample economies its correlation with the Import Competition Index is slightly negative, at -0.039.

indices.label: Import Similarity Index, all-origin shares (ISI_prod)
indices.description: Equation (10). Each product's market share for the country is computed over imports from all origins, not only from China. This captures cases where China suffers an excess supply in goods it was not already shipping to that country. Correlation with the baseline ISI is 0.773.

indices.label: Import Similarity Index, China's global basket (ISI_broad)
indices.description: Equation (11). Similarity between what a country imports from China and what China exports to all destinations, not just the U.S. It captures products where Chinese capacity has grown but direct U.S. exports were already constrained, such as electric vehicles. It measures a distinct source of exposure: its correlation with the baseline ISI is essentially zero, at -0.005.

indices.label: Consumer Gains Index (CGI)
indices.description: Equation (14). The predicted percentage decline in the price of imported goods as cheaper Chinese supply is redirected into the country. It weights the product-level price shock by China's share of the country's imports of each good and by that good's share of total import spending. Read it as a decline in import prices, not in the overall consumer price index: the effect on households depends on pass-through and on how much of consumption those imports represent.

indices.label: Consumer Gains Index, long window (CGI_long)
indices.description: The baseline index rebuilt with 2018 market shares and tariff changes measured from January 2018 to September 2025.

indices.label: Consumer Gains Index, basic shock (CGI_basic)
indices.description: The baseline index with the model-implied price shock replaced by China's baseline export share to the U.S.

indices.label: Consumer Gains Index, basic shock and full coverage (CGI_basic_full)
indices.description: The basic-shock variant extended to every product where the transparent proxy can be computed.

indices.label: Consumer Gains Index, intermediate inputs (CGI_upstream)
indices.description: The index restricted to intermediate inputs, meaning products with an upstreamness measure above 2. Here the immediate beneficiaries are firms buying cheaper inputs rather than consumers. Correlation with the baseline is 0.887. For a fuller treatment of this channel, which accounts for input-output linkages, use the Sourcing Gains Index.

indices.label: Consumer Gains Index, final goods (CGI_downstream)
indices.description: The index restricted to final goods, meaning products with an upstreamness measure below 2, where cheaper Chinese imports translate most directly into lower consumer prices. Correlation with the baseline is 0.903, and gains tend to be larger than the baseline because China sits relatively downstream in global value chains.

indices.label: Consumer Gains Index, trade coverage (CGI_coverage)
indices.description: Diagnostic, not an exposure measure. The share of the country's relevant trade accounted for by products that enter the consumer gains index.

indices.label: Sourcing Gains Index (SGI)
indices.description: Equation (15). The predicted percentage increase in a country's exports as cheaper Chinese intermediate inputs lower production costs at home. Unlike the input-restricted consumer gains variant, it traces input-output links, using binary input-output connections to map each input into the downstream sectors that use it. It is a direct, first-round measure: it holds input shares, technology, wages, and non-Chinese input prices fixed rather than propagating the shock through a full Leontief inverse.

indices.label: Sourcing Gains Index, long window (SGI_long)
indices.description: The baseline index rebuilt with 2018 market shares and tariff changes measured from January 2018 to September 2025.

indices.label: Sourcing Gains Index, basic shock (SGI_basic)
indices.description: The baseline index with the model-implied price shock replaced by China's baseline export share to the U.S.

indices.label: Sourcing Gains Index, basic shock and full coverage (SGI_basic_full)
indices.description: The basic-shock variant extended to every product where the transparent proxy can be computed.

indices.label: Sourcing Gains Index, trade coverage (SGI_coverage)
indices.description: Diagnostic, not an exposure measure. The share of the country's relevant trade accounted for by products that enter the sourcing gains index.
